title: Work-in-Progress: An empirical study to understand how students use ChatGPT for writing essays and how it affects their ownership
venue: The Third Workshop on Intelligent and Interactive Writing Assistants (In2Writing '24)
extended_summary:
This workshop paper describes a planned study rather than reporting completed experimental results. The paper addresses two main questions: how students use ChatGPT during essay writing, and how access to ChatGPT affects students’ perceived ownership of the essays they produce. The motivation is that LLM-based writing tools are increasingly available in education, but the authors argue that we still do not understand how students actually integrate them into writing processes or how such use might affect feelings of authorship and responsibility.

The proposed intervention is a custom web-based writing platform that embeds a simulated ChatGPT interface alongside a text editor. The system is designed to log keystrokes, edits, timestamps, copy-paste behavior, user prompts to ChatGPT, and model responses. Participants would write an essay to a pre-selected prompt while optionally using the embedded chatbot, and then complete an exit survey about ownership and perceived usefulness of ChatGPT. The authors propose analyzing prompt types through open coding and examining how chatbot responses are incorporated into students’ essays.

The intended population is university students enrolled in an ethics and professionalism course at Virginia Tech, most of whom are described as third-year students. The context is a single university course assignment setting, with monetary incentives for recruitment. The study is therefore about undergraduate essay writing in higher education, not a high-school or secondary-school intervention.

Crucially, this paper does not report outcome data, inferential statistics, motivation scores, writing-performance results, random assignment, treatment versus control groups, or effect sizes. It is a study protocol / work-in-progress describing planned methods and expected contributions. Therefore it cannot be the alleged 2026 randomized controlled trial with approximately 25 plus 25 secondary students over 12 weeks, and it should be excluded from any quantitative synthesis of ChatGPT-based writing feedback effects in high school because it provides no completed trial data and is not a high-school RCT.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a workshop work-in-progress describing a planned study rather than reporting completed empirical research. It provides no analyzed sample, no results, and no test of causal impact; therefore it does not meet empirical credibility criteria for quantitative evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: Impact is unclear because no outcomes are actually reported. The paper cannot support any estimate of ChatGPT's effect on writing or motivation.

interventions.use_case: Embedded ChatGPT-based essay writing assistant within a custom writing platform that lets university students optionally query GPT-3.5-turbo while drafting an essay, with researchers logging prompts, responses, and writing-process traces to study ownership and usage patterns.
Conversational ChatGPT interface framed as an essay assistance chatbot that students can ask for help during writing, but not positioned as a full instructional tutor with structured pedagogy.

finding.finding_summary: This workshop paper does not report empirical results on writing quality, writing performance, or any literacy outcome. It only describes a planned future study of essay writing with optional ChatGPT assistance among university students, so no original statistics, sample, effect sizes, or comparative outcomes are available.
finding.measure: planned essay-writing process logs and essay text; no reported outcome data

finding.finding_summary: The paper proposes to study perceived ownership and attitudes toward ChatGPT via an exit survey, but it reports no collected data and no statistical findings. As a result, there are no original motivation, ownership, or engagement results that could support effect-size extraction or synthesis.
finding.measure: planned exit survey on perceived ownership and perceived helpfulness of ChatGPT; no reported outcome data
